prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its biologically active form that made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B041 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. After round 1 the case rests on a narrower and, I think, more defensible claim than the one I opened with. Holst established the incretin effect and GLP-1 action in humans, Drucker defined proglucagon-derived peptide biology and the therapeutic rationale, and Mojsov characterised the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, the step that made the hormone usable as a drug template. That chain is original, mechanistically complete, independently confirmed in large randomized trials in diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular and renal outcomes, and mature enough that recognition is timely. The chair's question is whether one citation can honestly cover both discovery and drug design with three names. I do not think it can without blurring two different achievements, so I would keep the citation on the discovery strand and let the therapies appear as the demonstrated consequence, not as a credited invention. The unanimity of the opening ballots is not my argument; the argument is the shape of the discovery chain.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains the real weakness and round 1 did not resolve it. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide form is contested with the Habener group, Habener is not among the credited names, and the supplied record does not let me adjudicate it. Leaving out Knudsen can fairly be read as leaving out the step that put the therapy into patients, and three colleagues, including the chair, hold that view with serious arguments. If the committee concludes that Mojsov's contribution is a shared priority claim and not a distinct necessary step, the Drucker, Holst and Knudsen configuration becomes the more defensible one and I would not oppose it. A prize whose third name depends on an unsettled priority question is also less clean than CAR-T with June and Sadelain, though that case has its own missing originator.

responses.point: The chair argues that Knudsen's protraction chemistry behind liraglutide and semaglutide is the step that made GLP-1 a medicine, and that a prize crediting only hormone biology omits the reason the discovery changed practice. He also accepts that Drucker, Holst and Mojsov is the cleaner basic-science trio.
responses.response: I agree with the chair that the acylation-based protraction is what gave the field its drugs, and that the Knudsen configuration is the stronger one if the citation is meant to honour translation. Where I stay apart is on what a citation can cover with three names. Drucker and Holst are physiologists whose work made the drug development rational, and adding one industrial inventor and no discoverer of the active peptide, or the reverse, merges two kinds of achievement either way. I weigh the discovery strand higher because the prize tradition rewards the finding that made development rational, but I accept this is a judgement of emphasis and not a scientific fact. Your own concession that a cleaner basic-science trio exists is what keeps me comfortable that we differ on framing and not on the evidence.

responses.point: Linnarsson shares the Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio but holds it with only moderate confidence and names Drucker, Holst and Knudsen as the more defensible fallback if the Mojsov priority question cannot be resolved.
responses.response: That is the fairest statement of the dependency, and I share it. My confidence in Mojsov is conditional on her contribution being the chemistry and characterisation of the active GLP-1(7-36) form, not first discovery of the hormone, and on that being a necessary step and not one reached in parallel by the Habener group. The supplied text does not let either of us test that against the primary papers, so neither of us can claim resolution. I therefore treat your fallback as legitimate, and I would move to it if the committee agrees that the priority question is genuinely unresolved. Until then I think leaving out a discoverer to include a developer needs the stronger defence.

responses.point: Perlmann prefers Drucker, Holst and Knudsen but says that if the discovery itself is judged the Nobel-worthy part, Drucker, Holst and Mojsov is the cleaner basic-science trio, and that a drug-development component would need separate justification. Perlmann also judged nusinersen a better candidate for a later prize than for this year.
responses.response: Your point that a drug-development component needs its own justification is the strongest argument for keeping the citation on the discovery strand, and it is why I do not treat a two-part prize as free. On B007, I accept your reading that the field-wide change from SMN2 antisense is narrower than for incretins or CAR-T so far, and that a small group developed nusinersen. I keep B007 only as an alternative because the mechanism-to-drug link is unusually clean, and I declare an interest in splicing that should make me cautious about weighting it. I do not take the view that it must wait, but I agree it should not displace a mature candidate with broad reach.

responses.point: El-Manira ranks B035 second on conceptual novelty, raises the absence of Eshhar from the CAR-T credits, and calls the choice between Knudsen and Mojsov in B041 a judgement call on which colleagues may differ.
responses.response: I agree it is a judgement call, and I would rather the committee record that than pretend the evidence forces it. On CAR-T, I now put more weight on your Eshhar point than I did in round 1. Dropping Rosenberg gives a cleaner June and Sadelain pair but does not repair the missing originator of the chimeric receptor concept, so B035 remains my first alternative and not a preferred prize. If the committee finds B041's third name unsettleable, I think the right response is to change the B041 trio, as Linnarsson proposes, and not to move to a configuration with its own credit defect.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's contribution is a distinct necessary step, the characterisation of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, or a priority claim shared with the Habener group, which I cannot settle from the supplied text.
Whether the committee prefers the discovery strand or the drug-development strand of GLP-1 within a three-person limit, and whether one citation can honestly cover both.
Whether the credit list for CAR-T (B035) is complete enough to stand as a fallback given the absence of Eshhar, with or without Rosenberg.
Whether the newest cardiovascular, renal and neurological indications should feature in the citation or be left as demonstrated consequences.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate. I repeat my disclosure of a field interest in RNA processing and splicing, relevant to B007 (SMN2 splicing) and B042 (Ire1/Hac1 splicing), and past co-authorship with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisen. None of the credited candidates is personally connected to me, and the round-1 exchange did not change this. Shared topic or institution alone does not require recusal.
